title: zazzle MCP proxy use cases
description: Putting the proxy between an MCP client and another MCP server.

entities.name: Use another MCP server with cleaned results
entities.description: A coding agent's MCP client starts another MCP server through `zazzle proxy`, and gets that server's tool results back cleaned.
entities.goal: Use another MCP server's tools while spending fewer tokens on their results.
preconditions: The MCP client is configured to start `zazzle proxy -- CMD ARGS` as a stdio server (or `zazzled proxy -- CMD ARGS` where there is no invoker).
CMD is an MCP server that speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC on its standard streams.
postconditions: Every tool and resource text the server sent has reached the client, cleaned where that made it shorter; each shortened text is kept for an hour for read-again when the proxy has an output store.
When the server closes its output the proxy exits with the server's exit code.

flow.action: Its MCP client starts `zazzle proxy -- CMD ARGS`; the invoker replaces itself with `zazzled proxy -- CMD ARGS`, keeping the client's environment and streams.
Parses the options and starts CMD as a child with its stdin and stdout piped and its stderr passed through.
Its client sends initialize, lists the server's tools and calls them, as it would talk to the server directly.
Copies each client line to the server unchanged, recording the ids of tools/call and resources/read requests.

Copies each server line back; an answer to a recorded request has its texts replaced by their cleaned form where shorter, with the settings the --config file gives its tool or the command line's, and each shortened text is stored with an `[r:ID shortened by zazzle]` item added after the result's items; with --log a line `zazzled proxy: tools/call NAME ~A→~B tokens` goes to standard error.
When the server closes its output, waits for it and exits with its exit code.

alternatives.condition: The server is a Streamable HTTP endpoint: the proxy is started with `--upstream URL [--listen ADDR]` and the client is pointed at `http://ADDR/...`.
alternatives.outcome: The proxy listens on ADDR (default 127.0.0.1:8808) and forwards each request to URL, cleaning JSON answers whole and event streams per event, keeping each client connection open for further requests.

alternatives.condition: The options are wrong, the --config file cannot be read or is not valid, or CMD cannot be started.
alternatives.outcome: `zazzled: ...` on standard error and exit 2; the client sees its server fail to start.

alternatives.condition: The answer is an error, belongs to a tool named with --skip or skipped by its --config rule (or is a resource read the resources rule skips), carries only structuredContent or non-text items, or cleaning would not save a token.
alternatives.outcome: The server's line is forwarded byte for byte.
